deep.reconstruction:
This page is not by Riemann. It is the last page (marked 'Seite 9', sheet 3) of an editorial/bibliographic note by Karl Hattendorff, dated Kerstlingerode, 1 September 1875. Hattendorff had edited Riemann's posthumous memoir 'Ueber die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung' (1867), and the note surveys later literature for Riemann's collected Werke (1876). The page contains no derivations. Its content is as follows.

(1) It ends a quotation of the title of a work (on the previous, missing page) about the minimal surface bounded by a 'doubly isosceles' skew quadrilateral. The author treats the problem of §18 of Riemann's memoir in a special case. That problem is the Plateau problem for a skew quadrilateral, solved by Riemann via conformal mapping and hypergeometric-type functions. The special case is the one where two adjacent sides are equal and the other two sides are also equal.

(2) H. A. Schwarz (Berliner Monatsberichte 1872, p. 3) first solved Gergonne's problem of 1816. Take a cube; the boundary of the minimal surface must lie in the cube's surface. The two non-parallel (skew) diagonals of a pair of opposite faces are prescribed parts of the boundary. Tédenat had wrongly arrived at the helicoid. He overlooked the free-boundary (transversality) condition: the surface must meet orthogonally those cube faces on which the boundary is not prescribed.

Modern restatement (my addition): put the cube at [0,1]^3 and fix the segments from (0,0,1) to (1,1,1) and from (1,0,0) to (0,1,0). Seek a minimal surface containing these two segments whose remaining boundary lies on the faces x=0, x=1, y=0, y=1 and which meets those faces at right angles. This is a mixed Plateau / free-boundary problem.

Tédenat's helicoid (my addition) can be written X(u,z) = (1/2 + u cos θ, 1/2 + u sin θ, z), with θ = -π/4 + πz/2. It contains both diagonals and has H = 0. Its normal is proportional to (sin θ, -cos θ, u θ'). On the face x = 1 this normal has a nonzero x-component in general, so the orthogonality condition fails.

(3) Hattendorff also cites Schwarz's paper on the second variation of the area of minimal surfaces (Berliner Monatsberichte 1872, p. 718).
errors: No mathematical errors on the page; it is a bibliographic survey.
The historical claim matches the standard account: Tédenat's 1816 helicoid answer to Gergonne's problem ignores the orthogonality (free-boundary) condition, and Schwarz gave the correct solution.
The precise page references (Monatsberichte 1872, pp. 3 and 718) were not independently verified.

results.what: Special case of Riemann's §18 skew-quadrilateral Plateau problem: a doubly isosceles quadrilateral (adjacent sides pairwise equal)
results.modern_name: Plateau problem for a skew quadrilateral (Schwarz/Riemann quadrilateral surfaces)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (general quadrilateral, posthumous 1867); Schwarz (regular tetrahedral quadrilateral, 1865); the special case to the author cited on the previous page (unidentified here)

results.what: Gergonne's cube problem: minimal surface spanning two skew diagonals of opposite cube faces, meeting the other faces orthogonally
results.modern_name: Gergonne's problem / Schwarz's Gergonne surface (mixed Plateau and free-boundary problem)
results.usually_credited_to: Posed by Gergonne 1816; erroneous helicoid by Tédenat 1816; solved by H. A. Schwarz 1872

results.what: Second variation of area of minimal surfaces
results.modern_name: Stability / second variation of area (Jacobi operator)
results.usually_credited_to: H. A. Schwarz (1872, and later the Weierstrass Festschrift 1885)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is Hattendorff's 1875 bibliographic note on post-Riemann literature (Schwarz's work), written for the edition of Riemann's Werke. It contains no mathematics by Riemann and reports well-known attributions.

checkable.sympy: u,z=symbols('u z',real=True); th=-pi/4+pi*z/2; X=Matrix([Rational(1,2)+u*cos(th),Rational(1,2)+u*sin(th),z]); Xu=X.diff(u); Xz=X.diff(z); n=Xu.cross(Xz); E=Xu.dot(Xu); F=Xu.dot(Xz); G=Xz.dot(Xz); L=X.diff(u,2).dot(n); M=X.diff(u).diff(z).dot(n); N=X.diff(z,2).dot(n); simplify(E*N-2*F*M+G*L)
checkable.asserts: Equals 0: Tédenat's helicoid has mean curvature zero, i.e. it is a minimal surface.
Gives (0,1,0), (1,0,0), (0,0,1), (1,1,1): the helicoid contains the two skew diagonals of opposite faces of the unit cube.
The normal's x-component (proportional to sin(th)) is not identically zero, so the helicoid does not meet the face x=1 orthogonally. This is the free-boundary condition Tédenat overlooked.

transcription_corrections: 'Tédenat' is consistent with the image (accent on the first e).
Struck-through word after 'für den' is 'Fall', correctly shown as deleted.
Place name 'Kerstlingerode' (near Göttingen) and signature 'K. Hattendorff' are correct.
